contentHtml:

4baseCare, a precision oncology company focused on building population-relevant clinico-genomic intelligence, is collaborating with Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK).

The company will integrate de-identified data from a select cohort of MSK’s curated clinical outcomes, which will be used to support and improve 4baseCare’s AI-powered oncology digital twin platform, OncoTwin.

The integration, together with 4baseCare’s existing Indian dataset, will give OncoTwin access to a combined evidence base of approximately 80,000+ patient records. These clinical records will support data-driven cancer treatment decisions across 4baseCare’s network of hospitals and oncologists.

The development builds on 4baseCare’s participation in MSK’s 2025 iHub Challenge accelerator programme. Founded in 1884 and based in New York, MSK is internationally recognised for its work in cancer treatment, genomics and clinical research. Its deidentified data covers a broad range of cancer types, bringing a substantial body of clinical and molecular information into 4baseCare’s precision oncology platform.

4baseCare’s OncoTwin is designed to create a digital twin of a cancer patient using their genomic and clinical information. The platform identifies patients with comparable disease characteristics in its reference datasets, including the MSK records, and examines the treatments, drug combinations and observed outcomes associated with those cases. This allows oncologists to consider how similar patients have been treated in clinical practice, alongside established treatment guidelines and their own clinical judgement.

Commenting on the development, Hitesh Goswami, Co-founder & CEO, 4baseCare, said, “This collaboration seeks to address a major challenge in cancer care. While advances in medical science have made cancer treatment more precise, oncologists still face difficulties in using the vast amount of information available from other cancer patients to determine the most suitable treatment for an individual. With OncoTwin, we want to make that pool of information useful to oncologists across the world. The integration of MSK’s deidentified patient data, alongside our growing Indian dataset, is a significant step towards that goal.”

Rick Peng, Lead-Digital Ventures, MSK’s Office of Entrepreneurship and Commercialization, said, “Building on our work with 4baseCare as a participant in our iHub Challenge accelerator cohort in 2025, we’re excited for this expansion of our contributions towards 4baseCare’s efforts for a common mission of ending cancer worldwide.”

4baseCare will also integrate OncoKB, MSK’s FDA-recognised precision oncology knowledge base, into its OncoTwin digital twin platform.

“By leveraging OncoKB’s expert curated knowledge of the clinical implications of cancer genomic alterations, OncoTwin will be able to incorporate evidence-based genomic annotations into its analyses, supporting more accurate, personalized treatment insights to help guide precision oncology decision-making,” said Brendan Laing, Digital Health Licensing Manager, MSK.

After the completion of data integration and the necessary security, privacy and regulatory compliance processes, 4baseCare expects to make the expanded OncoTwin platform available from January 2027 across its existing markets in India, Latin America and Southeast Asia. The company currently works with 1000+ hospitals and 2500+ oncologists across its network, providing an established clinical channel through which the genomic comparisons can be introduced.

4baseCare is also working to address the lack of cancer data from Indian patients in global research. The company plans to increase its genomic and clinical data to over 1 lakh patients in the next two years.
